name: taking turns
describe: One player acts at a time, in order; a move out of turn is refused with a reason; a clock for each turn; bots act on theirs.
pick: only one player may act at a time: board and card games, puzzles played in moves
ends: the rules or a board say who won

turnSeconds.description: Seconds a turn may take before the host ends it: rules.turnTimeout may play a move for that player, else the turn passes (0: no limit)

botThink.description: Seconds a bot waits on its turn before it acts

first.description: Who goes first: rotate (the lowest seat, then the next seat each replay), seat (always the lowest seat), random

late.description: A player who arrives mid-game: join (the end of the order) or wait (the next game)

show.description: The goal line says whose turn it is (off when a mechanic shows it itself)

textTheirTurn.description: Goal line on another player's turn ({name})

textNotYourTurn.description: Refusal when it is not your turn

hooks.name: move
hooks.args: (ctx, player, move) → nothing | the reason it is refused | { again: true }
hooks.when: the player whose turn it is asked for a move (ctx.turns.submit(move) on their copy): play it here

hooks.name: turnTimeout
hooks.when: the turn clock ran out: a move to play for them, or nothing and the turn passes

hooks.name: botMove
hooks.when: a bot's turn, after it has thought: the move it plays

notes: The kit keeps the order, whose turn it is, the turn clock, the "not your turn" refusal, the goal line and the bots' waiting: write move(ctx, player, move) and call ctx.turns.submit(move) from the player's input.
Keep the game's state in ctx.shared and draw from it on every copy; play each sound where the state changes (in update), so every screen hears a move.
round.seconds is a cap on the whole game, not its length: end it in check(ctx) when the game is decided.
promise: Players take turns, a move out of turn is refused, and the game ends with a winner and plays again.
